docs.title: Software Defined Radio (SDR) Laboratory
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation portal and report repository for Team-07 in the Software Defined Radio Laboratory course at the Department of Electrical Engineering.

Lab Portal Overview

This website contains all laboratory documentation, including pre-lab preparation, real-time measurement logs, raw .cf32 data analysis, and post-session reports for ADALM-Pluto SDR experiments.

docs.title: 📡 ADALM-Pluto Transceiver Specifications
docs.text:
• RF Transceiver Chip: Analog Devices AD9363
  • SoC Architecture: Xilinx Zynq-7010 (FPGA + Dual ARM Cortex-A9)
  • Frequency Coverage: \(325\text{ MHz}\) to \(3.8\text{ GHz}\) (default RF tuning range)
  • Reference Oscillator Accuracy: \(\pm 25\text{ ppm}\) TCXO
  • Network Configuration: Static IP 192.168.1.10 via LAN/USB

docs.title: 💻 Software Infrastructure
docs.text:
• Flowgraph Environment: GNU Radio Companion 3.10+
  • Offline Post-Processing: Python 3 (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib)
  • Hardware Interface Drivers: libiio & pyadi-iio
  • Documentation Engine: MkDocs Material with MathJax rendering
  • Source Control & Hosting: Git & GitHub Pages

docs.title: Lab 01 Report: RF Spectrum Monitoring
docs.text:
Course: Software Defined Radio (SDR) Laboratory [1] Team ID: Team-01 [1] Date: [November 3, 2026] Team Members : - Member 1: [SeyedParham Moghaddasi] — - Member 2: [Amirali Rajai] —

Hardware Specifications: ADALM-Pluto (AD9363 Transceiver, Zynq-7010 FPGA+ARM), IP: 192.168.1.10 [8, 9], Reference TCXO Accuracy: \(\pm 25\text{ ppm}\) [10].

docs.title: 1.1 Flowgraph Architecture
docs.text:
In the lab01_monitor.grc flowgraph, the Filter Configuration parameter of the PlutoSDR Source block is set to Off [2, 7].

Hardware Analog Bandwidth Configuration

Setting Filter Configuration = Off prevents GNU Radio from overriding the internal hardware analog bandwidth filters [2]. In Off mode, the AD9363 transceiver maintains its maximum \(20\text{ MHz}\) default analog RF bandwidth, avoiding unexpected spectral truncation at the edges [2, 11].

docs.title: 1.2 Question 1: Reliable Span and Sweep Step
docs.text:
• Edge Roll-off vs. Spectrum Center: Analog low-pass filters (LPF) and digital decimation filters inside the AD9363 receiver attenuate amplitude levels at the spectrum edges near \(\pm f_s / 2\) [12, 13]. Additionally, DC offset and Local Oscillator (LO) leakage introduce an artificial spike at the baseband center (\(f_{bb} = 0\)) [12, 13].
  • Reliable Span Ratio: The reliable frequency span is defined as the central 80% of \(f_s\), covering \([-0.4 f_s, +0.4 f_s]\) [13].
  • Sweep Step Relation: To perform wideband spectrum scanning without edge distortion, the frequency step between consecutive center frequencies is set to:
\[ \Delta \text{step} = 0.8 f_s \]

This choice provides a 20% spectral overlap between steps, allowing attenuated outer edges to be cropped while seamlessly stitching reliable central bands together [13, 14].

docs.title: 1.3 Question 2: Frequency Error & Reference Accuracy for GSM900
docs.text:
• Theoretical Formulation: Downlink GSM900 carrier frequencies follow the standard grid \(f_{\text{standard}} = 935 + 0.2n \text{ MHz}\) [13, 15]. The absolute frequency error \(\Delta f\) and reference clock error \(\varepsilon\) in ppm are expressed as [10, 13]:
\[ \Delta f = f_{\text{observed}} - f_{\text{standard}} \] \[ \text{Error (ppm)} = \frac{\Delta f}{f_c} \times 10^6 \]
  • Nominal Boundary: For the ADALM-Pluto's \(\pm 25\text{ ppm}\) reference TCXO [10], at \(f_c = 945\text{ MHz}\) [16], the maximum expected offset is:
\[ \Delta f_{\text{max}} = 945 \times 10^6 \times (\pm 25 \times 10^{-6}) = \pm 23.625 \text{ kHz} \]

Data Verification Requirement

The screenshot 2.6.jpg.jpg lacks explicit numerical markers on the GSM carrier peaks. To strictly comply with lab regulations prohibiting data fabrication [5, 17], exact observed carrier frequencies must be extracted offline from Team-07's raw .cf32 I/Q recording to compute the device-specific ppm error [13, 18].

docs.title: Section 2: Loopback Test with Known Signal
2.1 Flowgraph Setup
docs.text: The lab01_loopback.grc flowgraph incorporates a complex Signal Source connected to a PlutoSDR Sink transmitting a single tone at \(f_{tx} = +250\text{ kHz}\) with a transmitter attenuation of \(tx\_att = 60\text{ dB}\) and receiver gain \(rf\_gain \le 10\text{ dB}\) [19-21].

docs.title: 2.2 Question 3: Quadrature I/Q Sampling & Positive/Negative Tone Separation
docs.text:
• Separation Mechanism: The AD9363 receiver uses Direct Conversion (Zero-IF) with Quadrature I/Q sampling [3, 12]. The received complex signal \(x(t) = I(t) + jQ(t) = e^{j 2\pi f_{tx} t}\) maintains a \(90^\circ\) phase difference between \(I\) and \(Q\) channels [12]. This phase relationship preserves signal rotation directionality in the complex plane, cleanly distinguishing \(+250\text{ kHz}\) from \(-250\text{ kHz}\) in the FFT spectrum [3, 12].
  • If Only \(I\)-Branch Were Sampled: The resulting signal would be purely real: \(x(t) = I(t) = \cos(2\pi f_{tx} t)\) [3]. By Euler's identity:
\[ \cos(2\pi f_{tx} t) = \frac{1}{2} e^{j 2\pi f_{tx} t} + \frac{1}{2} e^{-j 2\pi f_{tx} t} \]

Real-valued signals possess a symmetric spectrum around zero frequency [3]. Consequently, both \(+250\text{ kHz}\) and \(-250\text{ kHz}\) inputs would produce identical twin peaks at \(\pm 250\text{ kHz}\), making sign identification impossible [3].

docs.title: 2.3 Question 4: Peak Classification via LO Shift Slope \(s = \frac{\Delta \text{label}}{\Delta \text{LO}}\)
docs.text:
During the LO shift test (\(f_c = 434.00\text{ MHz}\), \(f_{tx} = +250\text{ kHz}\)), spectral peaks are classified using their shift slope \(s = \frac{\Delta \text{label}}{\Delta \text{LO}}\) [3, 22]:

  1. Real Transmitted Signal Peak (\(434.250\text{ MHz}\)):
  2. The physical RF frequency remains unchanged at \(f_{\text{RF}} = f_c + f_{tx} = 434.250\text{ MHz}\) [19, 22].
  3. Slope: \(s = 0\) \(\rightarrow\) Real Input Signal [3].
  4. LO Leakage / DC Offset Peak (\(434.000\text{ MHz}\)):
  5. Located at baseband DC (\(f_{bb} = 0\)), labeled at \(f_{\text{label}} = f_{\text{LO}}\) [12, 23]. As LO shifts by \(\Delta \text{LO}\), the label moves by the exact same amount [23].
  6. Slope: \(s = +1\) \(\rightarrow\) Receiver Artifact (DC Offset / LO Leakage) [3].
  7. Image Peak (\(433.750\text{ MHz}\)):
  8. Caused by I/Q gain and phase imbalance at the image frequency \(-f_{tx}\) [12, 24].
  9. Slope: \(s = -1\) \(\rightarrow\) Receiver Artifact (Image Peak) [3].

Anomalous Screenshot Observation in 100k.png

In image 100k.png, the main peak label displays \(433.996\text{ MHz}\) instead of \(434.250\text{ MHz}\) (\(s=0\)). This anomaly occurred due to a transient GUI parameter update during screenshot capture and is documented in the Troubleshooting section [6].

docs.title: 2.4 Question 5: Error Cancellation in Loopback Measurement
docs.text:
Clock Synchronization Mechanics

In over-the-air reception, transmitter and receiver operate on independent clock sources, exposing reference frequency offset [3, 10]. In loopback mode, both TX and RX reside on the same AD9363 chip inside ADALM-Pluto, sharing a single TCXO reference oscillator [3, 9].

Assuming a fractional reference oscillator error \(\delta\):

\[ f_{\text{TX, real}} = (f_c + f_{tx})(1 + \delta) \] \[ f_{\text{RX, LO}} = f_c (1 + \delta) \] \[ f_{bb, \text{meas}} = f_{\text{TX, real}} - f_{\text{RX, LO}} = f_{tx}(1 + \delta) \]

The software frequency label applies the same clock scale:

\[ f_{\text{label}} = f_{\text{RX, LO}} + f_{bb, \text{meas}} = (f_c + f_{tx})(1 + \delta) \]

Because the software frequency axis scale and sampling clock share the identical reference, the error factor \((1 + \delta)\) cancels out relative to the nominal software grid, yielding an exact reading of \(434.250\text{ MHz}\) [3, 24].

docs.title: Section 4: Troubleshooting & Anomalies
docs.text:
Anomaly / Symptom Suspected Cause Resolution / Fix Main peak label shifted to \(433.996\text{ MHz}\) in screenshot 100k.png. Unintended parameter range adjustment immediately prior to saving image. Verified raw binary .cf32 data offline using Python to confirm true peak at \(434.250\text{ MHz}\) [5]. Device or resource busy or No Pluto device found error in GRC console. Another active process or script holding IIO context open [4]. Killed background IIO processes and re-verified connection via ping 192.168.1.10 [4, 25]. Attenuated signal edges at high sample rates. Filter Configuration left on Auto instead of Off [2, 4]. Set Filter Configuration = Off in PlutoSDR Source block options [4, 7].

Quick Recovery for USB/LAN Connection Errors

If the GRC console outputs Unable to write attribute, ensure no secondary Python scripts or IIO sessions are connected to 192.168.1.10 before re-running the flowgraph [4, 25, 26].

docs.title: Section 5: What We Would Do Differently
docs.text:
1. Automated Sweep Scripts: Utilize pyadi-iio Python scripts for wideband scanning to eliminate manual tuning errors [27, 28].
  2. Strict Screenshot Protocols: Verify GUI parameter controls (\(f_c, f_{tx}, \text{lo\_shift}\)) immediately before taking screenshots [6, 7].
  3. In-Lab Raw Data Validation: Execute quick offline Python validation scripts during the lab session to verify file sizes (\(8 f_s T\) bytes) before disconnecting hardware [5, 18, 29].

docs.title: Section 6: AI Tool Disclosure
docs.text:
• Tools Used: Large Language Models (LLMs) were used for Markdown formatting, English language syntax polish, and LaTeX math expression rendering [6, 30].
  • Data Integrity: All analytical conclusions, numerical calculations, and code scripts were derived strictly from actual lab measurements and source documents [5, 17].

docs.title: Lab 02 Pre-Lab Report: Noise Figure, Gain Compression, and Intermodulation
docs.text: 📥 Download PDF Version of Pre-Lab Report{ .md-button .md-button--primary }

docs.title: 1. Summary of Theoretical Concepts
docs.text: RF receiver architectures are bounded at lower signal levels by thermal and internal component noise, and at upper levels by non-linear gain saturation and intermodulation distortion.

docs.title: Noise Figure (\(NF\)) and Noise Temperature (\(T_e\))
docs.text:
The Noise Factor (\(F\)) and Noise Figure (\(NF\)) measure the degradation of the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (\(SNR\)) as a signal propagates through a receiver processing chain:

\[F = \frac{SNR_{\text{in}}}{SNR_{\text{out}}} = 1 + \frac{T_e}{T_0}, \quad NF = 10 \log_{10}(F)\]

The input-referred noise floor (\(N_{\text{floor}}\)) over bandwidth \(B\) is expressed as:

\[N_{\text{floor}} = -174\text{ dBm/Hz} + NF + 10 \log_{10}(B)\]

docs.title: Y-Factor Noise Measurement Method
docs.text:
The Y-Factor method utilizes a calibrated noise source operating in two states: OFF (\(T_c \approx T_0\)) and ON (\(T_h \gg T_0\)), defined by Excess Noise Ratio (\(ENR\)):

\[ENR = \frac{T_h - T_0}{T_0}, \quad Y = \frac{T_h + T_e}{T_0 + T_e} \implies F = \frac{ENR}{Y - 1}\]

docs.title: Y-Factor Simulation Results (\(lab02\_sim.grc\))
docs.text:
• At Receiver Gain = 40.0 dB: \(N_{\text{off}} = -41.85\text{ dBFS}\), \(N_{\text{on}} = -32.78\text{ dBFS} \implies Y = 9.07\text{ dB} \implies \mathbf{NF \approx 6.50\text{ dB}}\)
  • At Receiver Gain = 10.0 dB: \(N_{\text{off}} = -51.40\text{ dBFS}\), \(N_{\text{on}} = -51.10\text{ dBFS} \implies Y = 0.30\text{ dB} \implies \mathbf{NF \approx 26.46\text{ dB}}\)

docs.title: Linearity & Intermodulation Results
docs.text:
• Single-Tone 1-dB Compression Point (\(G = 0.0\text{ dB}\)): \(P_{1\text{dB, in}} \approx -23.3\text{ dBm}\) (output reaches \(+0.24\text{ dBFS}\)).
  • Two-Tone Intermodulation (\(G = 0.0\text{ dB}, P_{\text{in}} = -30\text{ dBm}\)): Fundamental output = \(-25.79\text{ dBFS}\), IM3 products = \(-10.00\text{ dBFS} \implies \mathbf{IIP_3 \approx -37.9\text{ dBm}}\).
